_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 2 Science unit lecture film, Lesson 2 Teeth and Staying Healthy. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow LESSON['lecture'] in content/lesson-2.py part by part, under its own headings (three kinds of teeth; brushing; sugar and teeth; a healthy body; when you are ill), in the lesson's own words and examples: its tap figure of the mouth (ART.figure mouth, one kind of tooth named at a time), the apple, meat and peanuts of its tooth-jobs step, the pea of paste, gentle circles and two minutes of its brushing demo (the kit's toothbrush), the sweets, fizzy drinks, water and fruit of its sort, and the fever, cough, runny nose and tiredness of its signs of illness, with the faces its demo shows. People are brown (renderer.skin); the lesson's illness faces are smileys and stay yellow.
title: Teeth and Staying Healthy
subtitle: Grade 2 Science
objectives: Identify the different types of human teeth, explain how they are suited to their functions and describe how to care for teeth.
Know that humans need to manage diet, maintain hygiene and move regularly to be healthy.
Describe what illness is and describe the common signs of illness in humans.

beats.say: Your teeth cut, tear and grind your food.
Look after them, and keep your whole body healthy too.
Open wide. You have three kinds of teeth. Each has a shape that fits its job.
At the front are the incisors. They are flat, and they cut.
Beside them are the canines. They are pointed, and they tear.
At the back are the molars, big and wide, with bumps.
Molars grind and mash your food into small pieces.
Bite an apple. The front teeth cut a piece off. The back teeth chew it.
A toothbrush is a tool. It only works if you use it the right way.
Brush twice a day: in the morning, and before bed.
Squeeze a pea-sized blob of toothpaste onto the brush.
Brush in small, gentle circles. Do the front teeth, then the sides.
Then the tops of the molars. Keep going for two whole minutes.
Germs are tiny living things. They are too small to see.
Sugar feeds the germs in your mouth. Then they make holes in your teeth.
Having sweets and fizzy drinks every day can cause holes.
Water and fruit are kinder to your teeth.
A treat now and then is fine. Every day, all day, is not.
Three things keep your body healthy: good food, keeping clean, and moving.
Your diet is everything you eat and drink. Fruit and vegetables are good food.
Wash your hands before you eat. It keeps germs out of your mouth.
Move every day. Run, play and climb! It keeps your heart and muscles strong.
Then rest. Drink water, and have a good night's sleep.
Being ill means your body is not working as it should.
Often, germs have got in. There are signs you can see and feel.
A hot forehead is a fever. You may feel shivery.
A cough, a runny nose, or feeling very tired. These are signs too.
Do not hide it. Tell a grown-up, so you get better sooner.
Rest and drink water. Your body will mend.
Incisors cut, canines tear, and molars grind.
Brush twice a day for two minutes, and have sweets less often.
Good food, keeping clean and moving keep your body healthy.
If you feel ill, tell a grown-up. Your body will mend.
